notes: The supplied description and page do not specify the model term, emotion/error category, or comparison needed to identify a unique target. No target was assigned from audit ID, input order, or numeric matching. All statistics below are candidates only; none is a row-specific extraction. Emotion discrimination accuracy post-hoc d candidates on p.5: happy AN versus MD t35.2 = 2.6, p = .013, d = .73; sad AN versus MD t50 = 2.7, p = .010, d = .74; afraid AN versus MD t50 = 2.7, p = .009, d = .75; afraid AN versus HC t61.0 = 3.4, p = .001, d = .84. No emotion or group contrast is specified by the input. Page 5 also contains misclassification post-hoc d values .71 and .82. Candidate participant counts: the explicitly separate final HC, AN, and MD groups contain 37, 26, and 26 girls. For a three-group critical ANOVA, 37 + 26 + 26 = 89 participants; for AN versus MD, 26 + 26 = 52; for HC versus AN or HC versus MD, 37 + 26 = 63. These are conditional candidate analytic sums, not selected row N values. Medication sensitivity exclusions were nine AN and seven MD participants, but the paper reports findings based on the whole sample. No N was inferred from degrees of freedom. Original fields only were assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. PDF pages 4–6 rendered and visually inspected; canonical text is the evidence source. No effect-size conversions performed. Evidence fragments follow canonical text order: PDF p.5 top-right continuation precedes bottom-left paragraph in the supplied text; the rendered page establishes visual reading order.
